images.alt: An IBM Personal System/2 Model 30 286 desktop computer with its keyboard
images.caption: OS/2 was born on IBM's PS/2 line: the Model 30 286 belongs to the family of machines the joint IBM/Microsoft project targeted before IBM continued OS/2 alone.
images.author: DigitalIceAge

images.alt: An IBM PS/2 Model P70 portable computer, a boxy luggable with a built-in plasma screen
images.caption: The luggable PS/2 P70 shows the range of IBM-branded hardware OS/2 was built to run on, from desktop towers to field-portable workstations.
images.author: Wikström, Johan

images.alt: An IBM ThinkPad 701C laptop, closed, showing its compact black case
images.caption: IBM's ThinkPad line, introduced in 1992, was the flagship hardware for IBM's own operating system through the OS/2 Warp years of the mid-1990s.
images.author: nakashi

images.alt: Close-up of the IBM ThinkPad 701C's expanding butterfly keyboard, unfolded to full width
images.caption: The ThinkPad 701C's butterfly keyboard expanded past the width of its own case when opened, IBM engineering showmanship on the same machines that shipped with OS/2.
images.author: Raymangold22

images.alt: A CD-ROM disc for OS/2 Warp 4 installation media
images.caption: Warp 4, released in 1996, shipped on CD-ROM as IBM's last major consumer push for OS/2 against the coming wave of Windows 95 and NT desktops.
images.author: Asanagi
